title: Phishing and malware triage
description: Handling the alerts SOCs see most: suspicious emails and the malware they carry. Email header analysis, safe URL and attachment checks, sandbox use, handling user reports, signs of account compromise, containment and reporting - practised in a phishing triage lab, all from the defender's side.

lessons.title: Email header analysis
lessons.summary: Interpret message headers and authenticate the source of each observation.
objectives: Identify trusted Received hops
Distinguish envelope, signing and visible From identities
Explain alignment and document next verification steps

lessons.title: URL and attachment checks
lessons.summary: Triage suspicious links and attachments from preserved artifacts without opening them on an analyst workstation.
objectives: Separate display text from the recorded destination
Interpret static file metadata with its limitations
Route evidence to the approved analysis environment

lessons.title: Sandbox use
lessons.summary: Interpret sandbox observations with attention to coverage, privacy and provenance.
objectives: Trace observations to their monitoring source
Explain the limits of a single execution report
Make a policy-based decision about sample handling

lessons.title: User reports
lessons.summary: Receive user-reported phishing and turn the initial report into an actionable incident record.
objectives: Preserve the original submission and record user actions
Prioritise reports by observed interaction and possible impact
Close the feedback loop with the reporter

lessons.title: Account compromise signs
lessons.summary: Correlate account activity across sign-in, mailbox, endpoint and network telemetry.
objectives: Distinguish deviations from confirmed compromise
Correlate account and device evidence across sources
Document gaps and justify escalation

lessons.title: Containment
lessons.summary: Recommend and verify scoped containment for suspicious mail, accounts and endpoints.
objectives: Choose controls based on confirmed exposure and activity
Preserve evidence and obtain decision authority
Verify effective containment and record residual risks

lessons.title: Reporting
lessons.summary: Write audience-appropriate phishing incident reports with clearly bounded claims.
objectives: Separate observed facts from assessments and scope limits
Present time-sensitive decisions with owners and evidence
Preserve the source record and adapt distribution to each audience

lessons.title: Phishing lab
lessons.summary: Apply the module workflow to Banyan's synthetic phishing case using the course kit.
objectives: Preserve and evaluate evidence from the fictional case
Infer bounded scope from the dataset
Produce a defensible containment recommendation and incident report
